text:
sara: quick follow-up from the RFC — I sketched a 'stratified debt winddown' proposal for service-level paydown lanes. TL;DR: break tech debt into 3 lanes (hotpath, midpath, coldpath) and schedule paydown waves per lane + guardrail checks.

tim: +1. can you show an example lane mapping?

sara: sure — example mapping i suggested: hotpath = request-router, session-mesh, kv-cache; midpath = enrichers, routing adapters; coldpath = admin tools, report generators.

marta: sounds reasonable. how are we gating a lane completion? do we require perf regressions < 5% and no customer-facing errors for 2 weeks?

sara: yes, gate = unit/integ tests green + perf delta <= 5% on canary + no severity>=P2 incidents for 14 days. also require rollout runbook and rollback steps.

jordan: who owns the hotpath lane? @tim?
tim: i can take it but will need assistance from infra for KV and from runtime for batching changes.

marta: can we be concrete about small deliverables? otherwise it stalls. propose: 1) list top-5 debt items per service; 2) quick cost/latency estimate; 3) migration script or feature-flag plan.

sara: agreed. i'll own the coordination doc. i'll create a tracking sheet and add columns: service, owner, lane, risk, rollback, estimated dev days.

eng-bot: deploy-checker: canary window recommended = 2 hours with synthetic load; auto-rollback threshold = 7% latency regression.

jordan: agree with canary window. for hotpath we should require shadow testing on prod traffic before full cutover.

olivia: small ask — ensure any API contract changes have adapters for Dedicated/private deployments (some customers pin older clients).

tim: noted. adapters == thin facade that translates old request shape -> new. low-risk.

marta: schedule-wise: propose wave 1 (hotpath) = 6 weeks, wave 2 (midpath) = 4 weeks, wave 3 (coldpath) = 2 weeks. overlaps allowed if dependencies are isolated.
sara: that's the initial timeline i had in mind. we should reserve a 2-week buffer per wave for rollback and post-mortem.
jordan: question on metrics: what success signals do we capture? proposed: 1) 99p latency delta; 2) cpu/gpu cost per 1k requests; 3) error rate; 4) infra ops oncall pages.
sara: add eval regression check (quality) for any change that touches model-serving paths. we don't want accidental quality drops when optimizing batching/kv.

marta: ops request — include a short migration script stub in PRs. example: `./migrate_lane.sh --service request-router --dry-run` so infra can simulate state transitions.
jordan: put the stub in repo `infra/migrations/`. call out required env vars in PR description.

eng-bot: reminder: create canary dashboard (per-service) + link in runbook. template: `dashboards/canary-template.json`

olivia: cross-team caveat: Private deploys need a separate rollout checklist (no automatic canary on our prod fleet). we need manual approval steps.
sara: noted — i'll add a private-deploy checklist and mark owners for approvals.

marta: next actions: sara to create sheet + runbook template by EOD Friday; owners to populate top-5 debt items within 1 week; tim to draft migration script example this week.
jordan: i'll sync with infra to reserve canary capacity.
sara: thanks all. i'll post the doc link when ready. feel free to comment inline on the sheet once i share. :raised_hands:

tim: thanks — quick question: do we want to prioritise cost-yielding items first (big wins) or low-risk small fixes?
sara: hybrid — wave 1 should focus on high-impact, low-risk items first. leave high-risk for later once we have guards.

marta: noted. i'll help triage the list once it's up.

eng-bot: incident-tracker: created a placeholder issue for 'stratified-debt-winddown' in the backlog.

sara: perfect. closing for now — will reopen thread with doc link.
